_README: The MPC SOS Fade bot on the MT5_FFT terminal (PU Prime demo). This file is the ONLY thing that decides which terminal, account, symbol and strategy VERSION this bot trades — nothing is read from strategies/python/mpc_sos_fade/config.py, so lab experiments cannot reach it. No secrets live here: the MT5 password is in algos/credentials.json under mt5_accounts, and Telegram routing falls back to the shared group. The account MOVED from the Standard demo to the ECN demo on 2026-08-12 — read _moved_to_ecn FIRST, and note that _measured below is STALE because it describes the account this bot left.
_moved_to_ecn: 2026-08-12, Aaron's call. This bot traded account 700107749 (PU Prime MT5 STANDARD, symbol XAUUSD.s) from 2026-08-05 until today and now trades 700152905 (PU Prime MT5 ECN, symbol XAUUSD.p) on the same MT5_FFT terminal. The decision is measured, not preferred: docs/BROKER_QUESTIONS.md 2026-08-10 read all three tiers off our own terminals with a paired Standard control, and Prime and ECN are the SAME account with two commission rates -- same symbol, same $0.12 spread, same -79.60/+30.25 swap, same 20-point stops level, byte for byte -- so the cheaper toll wins outright with no trade-off to weigh. Round-trip cost per ounce: Standard $0.31 spread + $0.00 commission = $0.31; Prime $0.12 + $0.07 = $0.19; ECN $0.12 + $0.02 = $0.14. A 'no commission' account is not free, it is a marked-up spread. Replayed over 155,531 M15 bars: Standard 156 trades / +141.87R, ECN 157 / +151.39R. WARNING - the Prime-vs-ECN gap is 1.16R against this strategy's run-to-run spread of sd 15.06R, so ECN is chosen for being STRICTLY CHEAPER at identical everything else, never on that number. WARNING - the $0.12 spread is STATED, not measured: it came from five minutes of one quiet Asian session and backtest/fills.py still carries SPREAD_UNMEASURED for every raw tier. Leaving this terminal on ECN is what finally closes that -- run algos/tools/broker_facts.py --history-days 1 once a full day of ticks has accumulated. WARNING - COMMISSION IS NOW A REAL COST THIS BOT PAYS ($1.00 per side per lot = $0.02 per ounce round turn), where on Standard it was $0.00. It is booked on the entry deal and the exit deal, and mt5_ops.get_deal_breakdown() reports it separately from gross and swap, so the ledger's pnl_usd stays NET and correct without any change. WARNING - the old account's balance and trade history do not come with it; 700107749 is left as it stands.
_measured: ✅ RE-MEASURED 2026-08-14 ON THE ACCOUNT THIS BOT ACTUALLY TRADES, which is what the previous version of this block asked for. broker_facts.py --bot mpc_sos_fade_demo --history-days 6 (read-only, live MT5_FFT terminal, account assertion passed). Account 700152905 / PUPrime-Demo / USD / balance 9996.99 / PU Prime Ltd / leverage 500 / margin_so_call 120.0 / margin_so_so 50.0 / fifo_close False. XAUUSD.p: digits 2, point 0.01, contract 100 oz, tick value $1.00, tick size 0.01, volume 0.01-100.00 step 0.01, freeze level 0, spread_float True. SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL = 20 points = $0.20: the broker itself refuses a stop closer than that to the entry, independent of exec_min_stop_mode. SPREAD -- 3,033,270 ticks over 5 whole days: median $0.12 (12 points) / p90 $0.12 / p99 $0.18 / max $0.19 / min $0.11, flat at $0.12 in 22 of 23 traded hours. The only wide hour is the 22:00 UTC reopen after the 21:00-22:00 daily break (median $0.16, p99 $0.19) -- the same SHAPE the Standard account showed at $0.32, 2.7x tighter, which is what a raw tier sitting under a marked-up one should look like. Cross-checked against a 2-day window (1,280,613 ticks, unambiguously after the account switch): identical median and identical by-hour shape, so no Prime ticks leaked in. That check is NOT paranoia -- MT5 keys its tick store by SERVER, not by login, and both demos sit on PUPrime-Demo, so a window straddling the switch would silently average two tiers and look completely ordinary. This reading retired SPREAD_UNMEASURED for puprime_ecn in backtest/fills.py. SWAP -- long -81.18 / short +31.29 (a CREDIT), swap_mode 1 (points), rollover3days 3. 🔴 backtest/fills.py::_XAUUSD_SWAP still carries -79.60 / +30.25, i.e. 2.0% / 3.4% ADRIFT as of this reading, and was deliberately NOT updated in the same pass: moving a measured cost input re-prices every charged figure in the repo and belongs in its own commit with the affected numbers restated. This is the THIRD time this value has been caught drifting (2026-07-16, 2026-08-06, 2026-08-14) -- roughly 2% a month, with nothing anywhere announcing it. Treat swap as a rate that MOVES, never a constant. Server clock measured at UTC+3, the DST half of broker_tz_offsets '2,3'; the winter +2 is still UNVERIFIED. ⚠ STILL OPEN ON THIS ACCOUNT, and not answered by this run: FILLING MODE -- broker_facts.py does not read it, and a wrong one is retcode 10030 with the order simply not going on. COMMISSION -- not a symbol property, so MT5 publishes it nowhere on the spec; it lands on a filled deal. The $1.00/side/lot in fills.py was settled on 2026-08-10 by a 0.10-lot round turn read back through mt5_ops.get_deal_breakdown(), not by this tool. 🔴 SUPERSEDED: everything this block said before today was read off account 700107749 / XAUUSD.s -- a STANDARD tier this bot has not traded since 2026-08-12 -- and its $0.32 spread does not describe this account. Do not quote it here.
_broker_tz_offsets: MEASURED, not assumed: the terminal's tick clock read +3.00h vs UTC on 2026-07-31, which is the DST half of '2,3'. The WINTER half (+2) is inferred from the standard PU Prime schedule and is NOT yet verified — re-measure with backtest/tools/compare_feeds.py after the November changeover, because a wrong offset shifts every session boundary the strategy trades off and nothing downstream can detect it.
_account_risk_cap_pct: SET to 10% - Aaron's explicit call, 2026-08-09, ahead of a second bot on this account. It is the ACCOUNT-level ceiling on open risk across EVERY bot and every hand trade, measured to each position's CURRENT broker-side stop; exec_risk_pct is per-TRADE and had nothing above it until 2026-08-09. On this $2,000 demo account 10% = $200 of open risk for the whole account. WARNING - the cap EQUALS this bot's own exec_risk_pct, so with a second bot added the two do not share the budget, they take turns: one full-size trade or resting limit fills the entire $200, and the other bot is REFUSED until that room comes back. That is exactly the requested behaviour ('if there's no risk available to trade on, it should be blocked') and it is stated here because it is not obvious from the number - a cap that lets both trade at once would have to be 20%. WARNING - a RESTING order counts against the budget, unlike backtest/portfolio/, which reserves at the FILL. This bot enters on a limit that can sit unfilled for hours, so live contention will be MORE frequent than any stack backtest predicts; do not read the backtest's empty contention log as a forecast. WARNING - room comes back when a stop moves, which for this strategy is fast: A+ stages to breakeven on 161 of 161 backtested trades at a median of ONE bar. WARNING - this bot's OWN exposure is excluded from its own check, so the cap can never make it refuse its own re-size; it only ever refuses a bot that is not already on the book. WARNING - a position with NO stop REFUSES every order on the account, because unbounded risk cannot be measured and scoring it zero would hide the one thing this cap exists to bound. A hand trade left running is exactly that - check the account is clean before relying on this. WARNING - an unreadable balance or an unreadable account REFUSES; 'cannot ask' is never 'affordable'. WARNING - it REFUSES, it never SHRINKS, which is the opposite of backtest/portfolio/, so anything that tunes this number must be replayed under the REFUSE policy. NOT runtime-reloadable: changing it needs a restart, and until this bot is restarted it is still running UNCAPPED.
_exec_risk_pct: SETTLED at 10% - Aaron's explicit call, 2026-08-05. This field previously read 'DECISION PENDING ... harmless while the bot is in dry run', and both halves went STALE the moment the bot was armed the same day: it is live, and 10% is now a deliberate acceptance rather than an unexamined default. A comment claiming a live bot is not trading is worse than no comment. The number it accepts: 10% measured a -54.9% max drawdown over 6.5 years, and Run 12 established that the drawdown is a losing STREAK at this risk rather than give-back, so risk % is the only lever that moves it. On this $2,000 demo account, 10% = $200 risked per trade. Re-open this only if the account purpose changes from demo.
_exec_sl_deep: ON as of 2026-08-15, Aaron's call, and it is a DELIBERATE TRADE OF RETURN FOR DRAWDOWN rather than an improvement — read that before reading any number below. An entry that fills AT OR DEEPER THAN the 0.786 now stops at the leg origin (1.0) instead of the 0.886; 0.702 and shallower are unchanged. WHY: a 0.786 entry sits only 0.100 of the leg from an 0.886 stop, the tightest stop this strategy ever takes, and ordinary noise reaches it. MEASURED over 186,588 M15 bars (2018-09-13 -> 2026-08-10, XAUUSD 15m, bar fills, exec_secondary off), run through the UNMODIFIED strategies/python/mpc_sos_fade package: OFF = 182 trades / +140.0R / 58 full -1R stops (32%) / max drawdown 5.61R / 45.6% at exec_risk_pct 10. ON = 184 trades / +117.0R / 51 full stops (28%) / max drawdown 4.73R / 41.1% at 10%. So it BUYS 4.5 points of account drawdown and 7 fewer full stop-outs, and it COSTS 23R of return. WARNING - IT IS WORSE AT MATCHED DRAWDOWN: re-levered until its drawdown equals the 45.6% the shipped config runs at, it returns 3,830x against 4,868x, so dialling exec_risk_pct down to ~8.8% would have bought the same drawdown for less. This is on the record because a future reader seeing +117.0R against a +140.0R history will otherwise read a regression. WHAT PICKED THE 0.786 CUT-OFF, and it was measured rather than assumed: of the 58 full stop-outs at 0.886, only 19 (33%) were RESCUABLE - price poked past the stop, turned, and reached the trade's own TP1 before it would have hit a 1.0 stop. The other 38 blew through where the 1.0 would have been too, by a median of 0.177 of the leg against the 0.114 that separates 0.886 from 1.0. Split by entry level the rescuable share is 0.5: 30%, 0.618: 25%, 0.702: 22%, 0.786: 50% - so the trades worth widening for are exactly the ones entered closest to the stop, which is what this toggle already selects. WARNING - that split rests on 18 trades at the 0.786 and is the strongest entry-bar separator found in the whole investigation, which is not the same as being a strong one. WARNING - a BLANKET wider stop was measured and is much worse: 0.95 everywhere = +104.1R, 1.0 everywhere = +91.2R. The conditional form is the only one worth having. WARNING - 1.0 is the CEILING; config.py refuses a custom ratio above it, because 1.0 is the leg origin and the deepest level the fib ladder defines. WARNING - NOT runtime-reloadable. exec_sl_deep is not in live_config.RUNTIME_RELOADABLE, so this bot keeps trading the 0.886 rule until it is RESTARTED, and a restart re-checks the source-hash pin. WARNING - this is a PARAM change, not a code change: no promote is needed and none should be run for it.
_exec_min_stop_mode: ON at '% of price' 0.08 - Aaron's call 2026-08-05, after a 23-config sweep over 186,220 M15 bars (2018-09-13 -> 2026-08-04), ONE REAL REPLAY EACH (refusing a setup frees the single position slot, so the trade list reshuffles and no arithmetic over a finished list can stand in for a replay). Baseline 183 trades / +134.75R. 0.08 -> 181 / +136.75R (+2.00R). 0.10 -> 176 / +132.92R (-1.84R). 0.15 costs 25R, 0.30 costs 48R. It was briefly shipped at 0.10 earlier the same day; that was a measured mistake and this corrects it. WARNING - a small floor GAINS R for a mechanical reason, not a lucky one: the three tightest stops in 7.9 years ($1.03 / $1.06 / $1.18) were all full -1.00R losers, and Fixed $1.25 refuses exactly those three for exactly +3.00R. WARNING - do NOT read +2R as an edge. The jitter audit measured this strategy's run-to-run spread at sd 15.06R, so every value from 0.05 to 0.08 is statistically indistinguishable from zero and from each other. 0.08 is chosen as the HIGHEST value that does not start costing, i.e. the most protection for nothing. It is a SAFETY choice, not a profit one. WARNING - 'x ATR(14)' was measured and is the WRONG TOOL for this hazard: at 0.35 and 0.40 it never refuses the $1.03 stop at all, because that bar was quiet and $1.03 was not tight RELATIVE TO ATR. The hazard is qty = risk / stop_distance, which is pure price units - volatility does not enter it, so ATR blocks a different set of trades than the one at risk. WARNING - Pine parity is proven with this filter FIRING (block code 7 raised 213 times in a 21,899-bar export, compare_strategy.py exit 0 at warmups 100/500/1000/2000) but at 0.30, not at 0.08 - same code path, same px*val/100 floor, same refusal, same block code, only the constant differs. State it that way rather than claiming 0.08 was itself diffed. WARNING - it does not replace the two independent backstops: the broker's own 20-point SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL rejects a degenerate stop at the terminal, and place_pending_limit refuses one before it is sent. This guard is the one acting on OUR side of the wire, which is where the position is SIZED.
_account_profile: puprime_ecn as of 2026-08-12, matching the account this bot now trades (contract 100, mintick 0.01, commission $1.00 per side per lot, swap modelled). It is INERT live — it only prices fills when fill_model is 'tick', which the bridge refuses — and that is also why naming a profile whose spread is SPREAD_UNMEASURED cannot raise here: bar mode never constructs the profile at all (strategies/python/mpc_sos_fade/strategy.py returns before touching PROFILES). Set correctly anyway so the file never claims a tier this bot is not on.
_strategy_source_hash: Content hash of strategies/python/mpc_sos_fade as promoted in commit 8fb2986. The bot re-hashes on startup and REFUSES to run if the code moved. Newlines are normalised before hashing — without that the Windows VPS (core.autocrlf=true rewrites every newline on checkout) computed a different number for identical code and the pin refused to start every time; verified matching on both machines 2026-07-31.
_magic: Unique to this bot. Every order it places carries it and every order it reads back is filtered by it — this is what stops two bots on one terminal cancelling each other's orders. 770115 carries over to the ECN account unchanged — a magic is only ever compared WITHIN one account, and 700152905 has no other bot on it. ⚠ The 'MT5_FFT holds 0 positions and 0 orders' reading recorded here was taken on the OLD account on 2026-07-31 and says nothing about the new one; check the ECN account is clean before the first start, because a position with no stop refuses every order under account_risk_cap_pct.
_telegram: Both empty = the shared token and group from algos/credentials.json. Set telegram_chat_id to give this bot its own feed; set telegram_token_key (a KEY NAME in credentials.json, never a token) to give it its own Telegram identity.
